refuter_findings.evidence: The proof says, “In a local oriented coordinate frame,” but does not construct such a frame from the supplied orientation. The orientation definition gives a smooth orientation ray and defines an oriented chart by its coordinate frame lying in that ray; the proof must explain that an arbitrary chart can be adjusted by reversing one coordinate and then restricted to keep the sign fixed.

After noting that $Ae_0$ is future timelike, the proof concludes that “$A$ preserves the selected future component.” The cited cone result gives the two components, but the proof omits that an invertible Lorentz map is a homeomorphism of the timelike set and therefore maps each component to a component; this makes the conclusion follow from the image of $e_0$.

The proof asserts that the inverse-chart matrix entries are smooth because they are obtained from “the smooth frame vectors of $u$,” then later says in Proof 4.1 that the charts define the smooth structure. The frame-bundle supplier provides a topological frame bundle, and the smooth-principal-bundle definition requires a smooth total space. The proof needs to define the atlas using these local maps and establish chart compatibility before using smoothness of coordinates on $P^+_g(M)$.

The path uses $R_t=\begin{pmatrix}r^t&tz\\0&r^{-t}\end{pmatrix}$ for $r>0$, but gives no continuity justification for its entries as functions of $t$. The elementary identity $r^t=\exp(t\log r)$ supplies the needed continuity.

The path $t\mapsto B(tu)$ is asserted continuous although its entries use $\sqrt{1+t^2|u|^2}$ without a continuity justification. The proof also concludes from $B(tu)e_0$ being future timelike that the Lorentz map preserves the future component; this needs the short observation that an invertible Lorentz map is a homeomorphism of the timelike set and hence maps components to components.

The proof says that in the chosen basis $R_3$ is the displayed rotation, then interpolates its angle to obtain a path ending at the original $R_3$ without conjugating that path back to the original coordinates. It also states that a nonreal conjugate eigenvalue pair has product $1$ without spelling out that orthogonality forces its eigenvalues to have modulus one.

The derivative is defined as $[u,df_u(\widetilde X^H_u)]$ for $u\in\widetilde P_x$, without establishing independence of the representative. Replacing $u$ by $ua$ requires using right invariance of the horizontal lift and differentiating $f(ua)=\sigma(a)^{-1}f(u)$; the associated-bundle relation then gives the same class.

The text says, “With the defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$ chosen for spinor components,” but never specifies that representation's action, such as $\sigma(a)v=av$ for $a\in SL(2,\mathbb C)$ and column vector $v\in\mathbb C^2$. The preceding definition allows any smooth representation, so the spinor representation and resulting spinor-bundle terminology remain underspecified.

The Statement says “a $\mathrm{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$ construction” cannot lift the boost, but neither $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ nor this map is defined in the item or its dependency list. The only set definition of $SO(4)$ appears later in Facts & Assumptions, after its use in the Statement. The comparison group and map must be defined before use, or omitted.

The Statement asserts a uniqueness claim for “the Cartesian Minkowski tetrad,” and Verification 3.1 uses $e^I=dx^I$, but the item supplies no underlying manifold, coordinates, metric, or tetrad. Its Facts & Assumptions give only the quadratic forms and boost parameter; the sibling example is not a dependency. The claim needs data such as $M=\mathbb R^4$, standard coordinates, $g=\eta$, and $e^I=dx^I$.

reader_findings.evidence: The proof invokes a local oriented coordinate frame without constructing one from the supplied orientation. The cited definition gives orientation rays and oriented charts, but the proof does not explain why such a chart exists near each point. Reversing one coordinate of an arbitrary local chart and shrinking to keep the orientation sign fixed closes this short gap.

From A e_0 being future timelike, the proof immediately concludes that A preserves the selected future component. It should state that an invertible Lorentz map sends the timelike set homeomorphically to itself, hence sends the component containing e_0 to the one containing A e_0.

The proof calls frame vectors of u smooth before constructing a smooth structure on P^+_g(M). The listed frame-bundle dependency supplies a topological frame bundle, while the smooth-principal-bundle definition requires a smooth total space. Define the atlas using the local maps Psi_E and the overlap formula in Proof 3.1 before using smoothness of frame-coordinate functions.

The path R_t uses r^t and r^{-t} for r>0, but continuity of these functions is neither derived nor supplied by a dependency. State r^t = exp(t log r) and its continuity, or cite an exact real-power continuity result.

The asserted path t -> B(tu) requires continuity of sqrt(1+t^2 |u|^2), which is not stated or cited. The step also moves from B(tu)e_0 lying in the future component to the whole Lorentz map preserving it without stating the component-mapping argument. Both require short continuity and homeomorphism observations.

The axis/rotation argument omits the justification that an orthogonal 3x3 matrix with determinant 1 has eigenvalue +1, including the modulus-one fact for a nonreal eigenvalue pair. After choosing an eigenbasis, it asserts a path ending at the original R_3 without conjugating the displayed rotation path back to the original coordinates. Add these linear-algebra steps or cite an exact result.

The horizontal-differentiation formula is called a covariant derivative without checking independence of the representative u in the fiber. The dependencies give right invariance of tilde-H and equivariance of f, but the definition does not combine them. Differentiate f(ua)=sigma(a)^{-1}f(u), use invariance of the horizontal lift, and apply the associated-bundle relation to establish independence of u.

“Spinor components” and “the defining representation on C^2” are used without specifying the representation map or what qualifies as the spinor representation. State the exact action sigma(a)v=av for a in SL(2,C) and v in C^2, and specify which representation is being called spinorial before asserting the rank-two spinor-bundle conclusion.

The Statement uses SO(4) before its set definition appears later in Facts & Assumptions, and names a Spin(4) -> SO(4) construction/covering map without an exact definition or supplier in the item’s dependency closure. Define the comparison group and map before use, or state only the codomain obstruction. Clarify that SO(4) means the orientation-preserving orthogonal group for delta.

The item asserts a uniqueness fact for the Cartesian Minkowski tetrad but does not specify the underlying manifold, coordinates, metric, or tetrad. Verification 3.1 uses e^I=dx^I without defining its domain. The Facts & Assumptions only give abstract quadratic forms and the boost parameter; ex-gr-fx13-1 is a sibling, not a dependency. State M=R^4, its standard coordinates, g=eta, and e^I=dx^I with the connection domain, or remove this claim.
